claims.text: Tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy powders can be consolidated using spark plasma sintering.
The undoped SPS-produced tungsten-based HEA has established baseline thermal-conductivity and mechanical-property data.
Adding less than 2 wt% rGO to a tungsten-based refractory HEA will increase its effective thermal conductivity.
Adding less than 2 wt% rGO will preserve the structural integrity of the tungsten-based refractory HEA under plasma-facing reactor conditions.
Uniform dispersion of less than 2 wt% rGO in the HEA powder before SPS is an achievable intervention.
SPS at 700–800°C, approximately 50 MPa, and short hold times is suitable for consolidating the proposed rGO-modified tungsten HEA.
Thermal cycling from 800°C to 1200°C with cyclic mechanical loading simulates realistic plasma-facing service conditions.
The added rGO nanosheets will be uniformly located at grain boundaries and phase interfaces.
At less than 2 wt%, rGO will form a continuous interconnected heat-conduction network in the HEA.
Grain-boundary and interface-associated rGO will strengthen intergranular cohesion.
The intrinsically high thermal conductivity of rGO will create channels that dissipate localized thermal energy in the HEA composite.
Incorporated rGO can moderate strain concentrations, dissipate stress, and inhibit crack propagation.
rGO improves interfacial bonding in the tungsten-based HEA.
The rGO-modified HEA will have at least approximately 10% higher effective thermal conductivity than the undoped control.
The thermal-conductivity improvement will occur without loss of mechanical strength or ductility.
The rGO-modified material will maintain its performance during thermal cycling between 800°C and 1200°C.
Conventional undoped tungsten-based HEA intermediate layers have lower heat-transfer efficiency while possessing similar mechanical properties under comparable test conditions.
Keeping rGO below 2 wt% avoids the agglomeration and adverse microstructural changes expected at higher contents.
The intervention is expected to remain effective only within the stated 800–1200°C service range.
Extended thermal cycling may degrade rGO or its interfaces with the HEA.
